title: Insulating a concrete flat-roof garage
subtitle: Converting a cold concrete lid into a warm deck with PIR boards, without structural alteration
excerpt: A concrete flat roof on an integral or attached garage loses heat through the slab at roughly 3.5 W/m²K. Adding 80 mm of PIR board in a warm-deck configuration above brings that to around 0.25 W/m²K. The work is within DIY capability and requires no structural change to the slab.
sourceNotes: BBA (British Board of Agrément) certificates for PIR board flat roof systems. LABC guidance on warm-deck and cold-deck flat roof design. NFRC (National Federation of Roofing Contractors) guidance on re-roofing over concrete decks. BS 6229 for flat roof design principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat roof construction where the insulation is placed above the structural deck, keeping the deck warm and eliminating the risk of interstitial condensation within the roof build-up.
Polyisocyanurate rigid foam insulation board, the most thermally efficient rigid board available at 0.022 W/mK, typically foil-faced on both sides.
The vertical portion of a flat roof waterproofing membrane where it turns up the wall at the roof perimeter, forming a weather-tight edge.

content.text: A concrete flat-roof garage with an uninsulated slab is a heat sink for any room built above it, and for the garage itself if it is heated. The

approach places insulation above the existing concrete and waterproofing layer so the deck itself stays warm and avoids condensation risk. This suits garages where the existing roof is sound and merely under-insulated.

attrs.title: Building Regulations: Part L
attrs.body: Re-roofing more than 25% of a flat roof or improving the thermal performance of an existing roof triggers Part L compliance under Building Regulations. The required U-value for a flat roof on a notifiable job is 0.18 W/m²K. 100 mm of PIR (λ = 0.022) achieves approximately 0.21 W/m²K over a concrete slab; 120 mm achieves 0.18 W/m²K. Notify your local building authority before starting if the work is notifiable.

content.text: Assess the existing roof condition first

Adding insulation over a failing waterproofing layer traps water in the build-up. Check the existing surface for blisters, standing water after rain, and cracked upstands at the perimeter. A drum-like sound when walking indicates delamination of the existing built-up felt. Repair or replace the waterproofing before adding insulation.

The boards go above the existing waterproofing layer and are mechanically fixed or bonded in. A new single-ply EPDM or GRP membrane is applied over the top.
Board joints should be staggered; do not align joints between layers if two layers are laid.
The insulation layer raises the roof surface level. The

on the new membrane must be a minimum 150 mm above the finished roof surface. If raising the insulation level reduces the upstand below 150 mm, the parapet wall needs extending or the existing flashing needs refixing at a higher level.

A 20 m² garage roof at 3.5 W/m²K loses 70 W per degree of temperature difference. With 0°C outside and 15°C inside, that is 1,050 W continuously. Over a 3,000-hour heating season, that is 3,150 kWh. Adding 100 mm PIR drops the U-value to 0.21 W/m²K: loss falls to 189 kWh over the same season, a saving of around 2,960 kWh. At 2025/26 cap rates of 27p/kWh electricity, that saving covers the typical material and installation cost within 2 years in a heated garage. In an unheated garage the saving is zero but the room above benefits.

rows.symptom: Water tracks under the new membrane from the upstand edge
rows.cause: The upstand height is insufficient or the top flashing was not dressed into the wall cavity
rows.fix: The membrane upstand must terminate under a lead or aluminium flashing dressed into the mortar joint and pointed. Repoint or replace the flashing and ensure the top is sealed against wind-driven rain.

rows.symptom: PIR boards bow upward at the joints after installation
rows.cause: Boards were stored in the cold and expanded once warm, or they were not fully adhered down
rows.fix: Mechanically fix through the boards into the concrete with screws and large-diameter washers at 300 mm centres. Adhesive alone is insufficient on large areas in warm conditions.
